title: The White Brothers society band, the Bluebirds and the Smart Set
summary: The light-skinned society elite hired the White Brothers; when they could not play, Butler's Bluebirds played the Smart Set dances, which turned away darker guests, who went to Pythian Hall.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Now, the White Brothers they were a society band. Zeke ? was playing in that band, Harry White and there were four brothers, Harold White, Edward White, Sparky White, about four, and Zeke was in there, now all those boys, you see, you had to watch Washington during that time. Washington had what they called "high yellow" people and see, that society now, these people had all them good big jobs, man, and they owned all their homes and they was up there, so when these other people -- well, anyway, Harry White -- I mean White Brothers played for the Smart Set.

And when the White Brothers couldn't play for the smart set, well, the Bluebirds would come in and I joined the Bluebirds, and we played that pretty music too, and everybody was up there, looking pretty and and then everybody was kind of halfway yellow in there, see, but the thing when they're getting them dances, they'd have something over the door, I imagine there was something over that door, and if you didn't fit that thing, you wasn't getting in there. Or do you belong

to the club, well, no, I'm so sorry, but we can't allow you to come in but they had right next door the Pythian Hall, you may go in there. Oh, swell over there, and that's all them doctors and lawyers and things, see, so we up there playing there and them waltzes and all that beautiful stuff.
